answer.note: I read the code, not the ref files. All four ref files hold the same generic text, so they say nothing about priority. The incoming handoff named B and C. I changed that because the code points to D. Only dogwhistle/honest.py:175 `_verify_history` matches the request. It raises if prereg_commit == ledger_commit ("ledger seal must be a separate commit"). It also requires `git diff --name-only` between prereg and ledger commits to equal only the public digest file. I didn't check the "two-arm" part of the request. Suggested 60 minutes: honest.py 35 min (D). Read the verifier, its callers and tests/test_honest.py. Check edge cases such as the diff only comparing prereg to ledger commit, and renames. visibility.py 12 min (C). Its `_verify_history` at line 191 is a near-copy without those two checks, so it is the closest comparison. heldout.py 7 min (B) and study.py 6 min (A). Both have a three-commit `verify_history` (prereg, seal, ledger) with no equality check and no changed-files check. They are likely distractors. I picked C over B only because its code is closer to honest.py. That is a judgement call, and B is a reasonable alternative.
